title: A direct and non-invasive method for kidney delivery of therapeutics in mice
author: Pavathuparambil Abdul Manaph, Al-Hawwas, et al.

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse with ketamine
steps.instruction: Inject ketamine to anesthetize the mouse; confirm anesthesia by lack of movement when the tail or leg is pinched.

steps.title: Prepare syringe and mark needle
steps.instruction: Load a syringe with the diluted therapeutic (e.g., 0.5 × 10⁶ GFP‑tagged cells in 50 µL PBS) and place a mark 3 mm from the needle tip to set the injection depth.

steps.title: Position mouse and prepare surgical site
steps.instruction: Place the anesthetized mouse on a heat pad, shave hair at the surgical site using electric clippers or shavers, and wipe the skin with ethanol‑soaked gauze.

steps.title: Locate and stabilize kidney
steps.instruction: Palpate the flank to locate the kidney (visible after cleaning in white‑skinned strains such as NOD/SCIDS) and hold the organ firmly to prevent slipping.

steps.title: Inject therapeutic into kidney
steps.instruction: Insert the needle through the skin to the 3 mm mark, then slowly inject the solution, pausing 2 seconds for every 10 µL delivered.

steps.title: Repeat injection on opposite kidney
steps.instruction: If required, repeat the locating, stabilizing, and injection steps on the contralateral side to deliver the agent to the other kidney.

steps.title: Monitor animal recovery
steps.instruction: Observe the mouse until normal movement and behavior resume.

steps.title: Euthanize and perfuse organs
steps.instruction: One week later, euthanize the mouse with a single overdose of pentobarbitone, perfuse the kidneys with PBS, and fix them in 4 % paraformaldehyde.

steps.title: Section kidneys for analysis
steps.instruction: Cut 30–40 µm thick sections using a cryostat; transfer sections to PBS or antifreeze solution for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Prepare sections for microscopy
steps.instruction: Wash stored sections in fresh PBS, mount on glass slides, and image under a fluorescence microscope; for H&E staining, process sections automatically and scan with a Nanozoomer S60 (Hamamatsu).
